criteria.rationale: Premises checked rather than taken: run 38021679842 is CI on aa29027d with conclusion success, and its test job shows the journey step, the mirror step (printed ["https://mirror.gcr.io/"]) and Delivery images build and start all successful; release.yml line 25 calls ci.yml as a reusable workflow, so the Release run that failed with the 403 gets the same token.

Without GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN the journey sends no Authorization header; I ran POSE_JOURNEYS=1 TestJourneysInstallAndUpgradeFromThePublishedRelease with both unset and with a token set, and both passed. Both Dockerfiles pin golang and alpine by sha256 digest, so the mirror cannot change the image bytes.

install-and-upgrade-journeys-integration passed in the sealed run with POSE_JOURNEYS=1; the empty AUTH array is safe under set -u on the bash 5 runners, and the [ -n ] && assignment does not trip set -e.
The design delta has no material structural fact; the four changed paths are the spec, its start record, the journey script (R1) and ci.yml (R2 journey env, R3 mirror step before the image build).

Rules applied: security (the token is sent only as a header, never echoed; curl -fsSL prints no headers), delivery-evidence (R3 names the CI run, confirmed through the GitHub API), documentation-style. Each workflow step carries a comment naming the spec. D1 records the mirror-versus-login choice.

pose validate --tolerant: 131 step(s), 131 pass, Result: SUCCESS, no failing step and no waiver. Residual risk recorded in the spec: if mirror.gcr.io is down the daemon falls back to Docker Hub. Observation, not a defect: the step overwrites /etc/docker/daemon.json instead of merging, which the passing run shows is harmless on ubuntu-latest today.

R1 by the journey run with and without a token; R2 by ci.yml line 70 (GITHUB_TOKEN: github.token on the journey step); R3 by the mirror step at ci.yml lines 78-85, ahead of the image build, and by run 38021679842.

Reviewed both commits with POSE-Spec: pose-ci-avoids-anonymous-rate-limits (aa29027d, 51397624): 4 claims equal 4 observed paths, nothing outside the journey, the workflow and the spec records. The reviewer id agent:independent-claude-opus-5-5-review carries the independent- prefix only as the declaration the engine requires; this review is another execution of the same vendor and model as the implementer (Claude Opus 5.5, agent:claude-opus-5-5), run as a fallback because the other-vendor reviewer (Codex) was unavailable: independence of execution, not of vendor. The maintainer authorized this reviewer id.
No new secret: the workflow token under permissions contents: read; the token never reaches logs or files; the mirror serves digest-pinned images only. No credential appears in the diff.
An optional header and one daemon config step are the smallest changes that remove both anonymous limits; docker login would have needed a provisioned secret (D1).
